examples.japanese: {扉|とびら}を{開|あ}けると、{広|ひろ}い{庭|にわ}が{見|み}えた。
examples.english: When I opened the door, I saw a spacious garden.

examples.japanese: {重|おも}い{扉|とびら}を{押|お}して{中|なか}に{入|はい}った。
examples.english: I pushed the heavy door and entered inside.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{扉|とびら}を{開|ひら}くことを{恐|おそ}れないでください。
examples.english: Don't be afraid to open new doors (figurative).

notes:
{扉|とびら} specifically refers to a hinged door that swings open, as opposed to sliding doors. It often has a more literary or formal nuance than ドア.

Distinctions:
- {扉|とびら}: hinged door (literary, includes gates)
- ドア: door (casual loanword, common in daily speech)
- {戸|と}: general term for door/sliding door
- {障子|しょうじ}: paper sliding door
- {襖|ふすま}: opaque sliding door

Figurative usage:
- {新|あたら}しい{扉|とびら}を{開|ひら}く (open new doors/possibilities)
- {心|こころ}の{扉|とびら} (the door of one's heart)
